newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Currencies worry Canada,NZ.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Currencies worry Canada,NZ.

text.p: Short Australian bond yield spreads tightened to both Canada and New Zealand as currency concerns plagued both countries.

In particular, the New Zealand dollar came under renewed attack, meaning once again that the N.Z. debt market had to re-adjust to keep monetary conditions within the Reserve Bank of N.Z.'s desired level.
Just after the close, N.Z. Finance Minister Bill Birch told Reuters that he expected the N.Z. dollar to come down further.
"They (the RBNZ) are foreshadowing further easings towards the end of the year so you are likely to get a little more easing," Birch said.
The Canadian dollar also weakened on Friday as the market tested the Bank of Canada's resolve over a further tightening in monetary easing.

While the Australian dollar was softer on the day, this was on the continued expectation of a monetary easing by the Reserve Bank after its board meeting on August 5, which has been entrenched in the currency for sometime.

Local yield differentials to the U.S. were little changed, and some analysts still saw scope for a further compression in the coming weeks, and perhaps to parity following recent market-friendly domestic data and due to a subdued U.S. market.

"The bottom line is that benign summer trading conditions in the U.S. treasury market may give the Australian 10-year bond a shot a parity with U.S. treasuries at a yield perhaps around 6.2 percent," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS.
But "As stronger U.S. data come through in their (autumn), maintaining low six percent yields either side of the Pacific will become difficult," he added.
